morphology.shape: Crescent-shaped tachyzoite; spherical tissue cyst (bradyzoites); oocyst (in cat feces)

protozoanDetails.lifeCycleForm: Tachyzoite (acute, rapidly dividing), bradyzoite (tissue cyst, latent), and oocyst (excreted only by definitive feline hosts)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Domestic and wild cats (definitive hosts, sexual reproduction in the intestine); virtually all warm-blooded animals can serve as intermediate hosts
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic; humans are accidental intermediate hosts
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Oocysts shed in cat feces can persist in soil for extended periods
habitat.reservoir: Domestic/wild cats; undercooked meat from infected intermediate hosts (e.g. pork, lamb)

microscopy.stain: Giemsa stain of tissue or body fluid; histopathology of tissue cysts
microscopy.appearance: Crescent-shaped tachyzoites intracellularly in acute infection; cystic bradyzoite-filled structures in chronic tissue infection

identificationClues: Serology (IgG/IgM) is the primary diagnostic method in immunocompetent patients
PCR of amniotic fluid used for suspected congenital infection
Ring-enhancing brain lesions on imaging in reactivation disease (e.g. AIDS-associated toxoplasmic encephalitis)
Crescent-shaped tachyzoites seen in acute-phase tissue specimens

diseases: Lymphadenopathic toxoplasmosis in immunocompetent hosts (often subclinical or mild)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Ingestion of oocysts from cat feces-contaminated soil/food/water; ingestion of undercooked meat containing tissue cysts; transplacental transmission to the fetus
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common parasitic infections worldwide; primary maternal infection during pregnancy carries risk of severe congenital disease; reactivation is a classic opportunistic infection in advanced HIV/AIDS
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: IgM/IgG avidity testing helps date the timing of maternal infection relative to pregnancy to assess fetal risk

examFacts.importantTest: IgG/IgM serology; PCR of amniotic fluid for congenital infection
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Cats are the only definitive host capable of producing infective oocysts; humans and most other animals are intermediate hosts only
